title: Squaremas
statementMd:
You are given two integers 𝑚m and 𝑛n. Print a grid of integers with 𝑚m rows and 𝑛n columns such that the four corners of any rectangular subgrid add up to a perfect square. Each integer must lie in the range [1,109][1,109]. Note that we are only interested in rectangular subgrids that have four corners. Your solution must contain at least two different numbers. It can be shown that under the given constraints, a solution always exists.

An example on a 3×33×3 grid is shown below. Several examples of rectangular subgrids are highlighted. The four corners of each rectangle are colored red. Note that the entire grid is also considered a subgrid.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f93e9044f5fe1a5701fa117a52d4826031477d26.png)

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases 𝑡t (1≤𝑡≤501≤t≤50). The description of the test cases follows.

Each test case consists of a single line containing two integers 𝑚m and 𝑛n (2≤𝑚,𝑛≤1002≤m,n≤100) — the required number of rows and columns of the grid.

It is guaranteed that the sum of 𝑚m and the sum of 𝑛n over all test cases are at most 100100.

## Output

For each test case, output 𝑚m rows, each containing 𝑛n integers satisfying the above conditions.

If there are multiple solutions, you may output any.

## Note

The first test case is shown in the image below.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/99694dc0e0bca14444aee693128712036a7dcff8.png)

The second test case is from the image in the problem statement. There are 9 rectangles to consider. In all, we have

- 3+2+31+13=49=723+2+31+13=49=72
- 2+29+13+37=81=922+29+13+37=81=92
- 31+13+1+19=64=8231+13+1+19=64=82
- 13+37+19+31=100=10213+37+19+31=100=102
- 3+29+31+37=100=1023+29+31+37=100=102
- 31+37+1+31=100=10231+37+1+31=100=102
- 3+2+1+19=25=523+2+1+19=25=52
- 2+29+19+31=81=922+29+19+31=81=92
- 3+29+1+31=64=823+29+1+31=64=82
